growth_signal.value: Valued at $4 billion in January 2026, up from $2.1 billion in January 2025.

entry.idea: Making a video is slow and costly, so Synthesia lets people type text and get a video with a talking digital presenter.
entry.lesson: Replace a costly craft, such as filming, with software, then sell it to every company that needs it.
entry.name: Synthesia

growth.reason: The company says it has 60,000 business customers and its value nearly doubled in a year.

market.reason: Companies of every kind in many countries make training and marketing video.

tech.reason: Lifelike avatars and dubbing are solid engineering, but other video AI teams are close behind.

sources.title: Synthesia doubles valuation to $2.1bn and pledges commitment to UK
AI video startup co-founded by UCL Professor, valued at $4 billion
Synthesia becomes the UK's largest AI product

entry.twist: Its avatars speak 140+ languages, and users can now practise talks or run surveys with avatars that talk back.
entry.who_pays: Businesses pay a subscription to make training, sales and internal videos.
entry.why_now: AI can now make lifelike faces and voices, and firms want training and sales videos in many languages without film crews.
